comment.body:
Edward Snowden blew the whistle on illegal mass surveillance by US authorities of their own population – and had to flee into permanent exile.

Julian Assange published details of the US military's war crimes – and spent years locked up in a high-security jail, denied his most basic rights.

Francesca Albanese has documented US government and corporate complicity in Israel's genocide in Gaza – and now, thanks to US sanctions, cannot have a bank account. As she explains here, anyone who deals with her faces up to 20 years in a US jail.

Notice a pattern? The US is the ultimate rogue state, destroying anyone who tries to hold it to account. It is utterly lawless. Its methods are those of the gangster, ruling a world where there are no police who can bring it to heel.

Trump is different only in that he no longer bothers to hide the fact.

comment.name: Millard J Melnyk
comment.body:
Obviously. 



But to get out of the loop, you'd first have to credibly envision a world without rulers. 



And fucking no one has done that yet, not even the anarchists. 



Here's one of the non-optional characteristics of a world without rulers: no ownership. 



Not common ownership, shared ownership, gifting, or any of the other alternatives that absolutely do not break out of the ownership paradigm. 



No ownership, period. 



And before you think it I'll tell you what your next thought will be: how could that work? 



Before you have a hope of answering that question, you need to fix the problems in your thinking -- and for that matter in your heart -- because that question isn't rational, it's triggered. 



That's why everybody asks it, almost verbatim. 



I've been working at this for decades, and that's always the question where people's thinking stops. It's a conditioned reflex, because they just sit there waiting for someone else to give them an answer. And, unless someone does, they idiotically assume there must not be an answer.



The fears that trigger that question need to be resolved before you have a hope and hell of answering that question.

comment.name: Millard J Melnyk
comment.body:
It's not tricky or difficult.

 

5 years ago, would you have believed where things are now?

 

That shows you won't believe where things will be 5 years from now, either -- and you'd be wrong.

 

I knew which direction things were going, and that's proven out. I had no fucking clue how fast and how far it would go by now, though.

 

To stop being wrong year after year, you'll have to change the way your mind works -- because your own experience proves, at any point in time, that you don't have a fucking clue what's really going on nor where it's headed.

 

But you'd have to be honest and look at yourself to see it.

comment.name: Millard J Melnyk
comment.body:
“Consent of the governed”.

“Politicians don’t care.”

“Politicians don’t hold themselves accountable.”

Holy bleeding Christ.

I don't argue that this vid won't help people who are severely cultized to start realizing, at a superficial level, the insanity going on.

 

The deeper problem is the psychosis required to make "consent of the governed" seem like a credible, coherent idea.

 

Sure, if you're already bent on being governed, it's the kind of bullshit rationalization you might come up with to make yourself look like you're not the sniffling codependent you actually are. But that's about it.

 

The merit of the idea is on the order of making your older brother the head of the household, expecting him to behave with the kind of love and grace and care and forgiveness that a good parent would demonstrate.

 

What the fuck?

 

OMG, now I'm at the part where the problem is that the politicians don't care? What's up with expecting psychopaths to care? Even worse, what's up with the kind of sniveling codependence that can't conceive of any solution other than getting psychopaths to care? 

Holy shit.

 

Now the problem is that politicians don’t hold themselves accountable.

Why would anyone in their right mind expect politicians to hold themselves accountable? And what's up with the psychosis responsible for thinking that it's a good idea to to put people in power who will abuse that power, always, unless we hold them accountable? Why not put people in power that we can trust? Why rely in the first place on a system predicated on the kind of power that just begs to be abused and that, to the degree that it's perfected, perfectly corrupts?

 

The only kind of mind that any of this could make any sense to is a mind that has been brutalized, conquered, enslaved, and has resigned itself that there is no hope for anything completely different. In other words, codependents.

comment.name: Millard J Melnyk
comment.body:
Love is just what naturally happens when you actually see a person for who they are. 



Unless you're too psychologically damaged -- seeing a human being for real, unretouched and uncontorted, is to behold someone precious. Appreciation and love, then, are as certain as gravity.



But you can't see them without simultaneously letting yourself be seen for who you really are. 



Our shame and self-loathing -- which force us to hide, to project personas, pretend roles, bullshit, and lie -- drive us into a deep, disastrous dishonesty. 



That dishonesty is why people feel abysmally alone, abandoned, lost. 



They've betrayed and abandoned themselves -- because the truth is: every single person, the real person underneath all the shit and bullshit, is precious, beautiful, and would inspire love in the hearts of everyone who saw them, if only they'd let themselves be seen. 



For fear of liars we become liars, and rather than brave the bullshit of the self-condemned, we choose utter isolation instead.



You don't feel lonely when you're seen.



In a world like this one, belligerent honesty is a revolutionary act.

comment.body:
Every single horrific act in the history of the human race has, ultimately, been the result of beliefs: supremacism, racism, xenophobia, self-righteous moralism, etc. 



You might argue that every single wonderful, good, beautiful, beneficial act in the history of the human race has, ultimately, been the result of beliefs -- but no, that's absolutely wrong. 



They've been the result of love, and love has nothing to do with beliefs.



But if you were right, then you'd have a big problem you'd need to explain: how the same cognitive act could be responsible for both the heinous and the beautiful. 



Oh, you say, but beliefs are neutral. It all depends on the believer. 



That just raises a different problem: how the mentality of the heinous could be the same as the beautiful when it comes to this thing called "belief".



If I showed you how you were thinking and doing exactly the same thing that a psychopath does, wouldn't you immediately wonder if there might be something wrong? 



Your thinking makes no sense -- at a psychosis-grade level of incoherence.
